project.name: Institute Evidence Integrity Search
project.primary_question: Does treatment-resistant depression meet the same evidentiary criteria that previously justified separation of diseases, endotypes, or stages?
coverage_limits: Web-accessible sources only in this pilot
No claim of exhaustive database coverage
No quantitative pooling unless studies are sufficiently comparable

competing_models.label: Distinct disease
competing_models.prediction: A stable pretreatment discriminator separates future TRD from responsive MDD and predicts distinct course or treatment interaction.

competing_models.label: Stage or severity
competing_models.prediction: Resistance probability increases continuously with severity, chronicity, recurrence, and accumulated illness.

competing_models.label: Multiple endotypes
competing_models.prediction: Several reproducible biological subgroups cut across the binary TRD boundary and show differential treatment benefit.

competing_models.label: Operational treatment-course category
competing_models.prediction: Membership changes materially with definitions, treatment adequacy, adherence, access, and diagnostic correction.

competing_models.label: Mixed model
competing_models.prediction: Stage, endotype, and pseudo-resistance mechanisms contribute in different proportions.

competing_models.label: Artefact or selection model
competing_models.prediction: Apparent biological separation is substantially explained by selection, treatment exposure, measurement, or selective publication.

shared_discriminator_questions: Was the feature measured before resistance developed?
Is it stable across time and treatment?
Is it specific beyond severity, chronicity, bipolarity, comorbidity, medication exposure, adherence, and socioeconomic access?
Does it reproduce in independent cohorts and diverse settings?
Does it identify a different natural history?
Does it modify comparative treatment benefit or harm?
Would using it improve clinical decisions?

appraisal_routing.omics_or_basic_science: domain checklist: multiplicity, batch, blinding, prespecification, replication, confounding, assay validity

claim_block_rules.condition: decisive citation or numerical result cannot be verified
causal language relies only on cross-sectional or uncontrolled association
companion publications or overlapping datasets are counted as independent
registered primary outcomes are missing or changed without explanation
subgroup or threshold was defined after observing outcomes
disease distinction is inferred only from a regulator-approved indication
exact search counts lack query, source, date, and export

human_gate_required_for: promoting exploratory subgroup to primary model

stopping_rule: Two consecutive cycles add no study family that changes a conclusion or confidence rating
New searches mostly return duplicates or represented evidence classes
Pivotal study-family citation mining is complete within available access
All sentinel studies are retrieved or misses are explained
All blocked central claims are resolved or remain explicitly blocked
